# ephemeral.docker_registry_login

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: ephemeral-resource. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Validates registry credentials through the daemon (`POST /auth`, like `docker login`) and returns the identity token the registry issues, if any. It is ephemeral: the token and the response are never written to plan or state. Nothing is stored on the daemon or in a docker config file. Without `username`, the provider's matching `registry_auth` entry is used.

Ephemeral resources need Terraform >= 1.10. Their values are never written to
plan or state; reference them only from ephemeral contexts (write-only
arguments, provider blocks, ephemeral variables, outputs and locals, other
ephemeral resources).

## Usage

```terraform
ephemeral "docker_registry_login" "<name>" {
  # arguments below
}

# Reference ephemeral.docker_registry_login.<name>.<attr> only from ephemeral contexts:
# write-only arguments, provider blocks, ephemeral variables/outputs/locals.
```

| `username` | `string` | optional, computed |  |  | User name. Omitted: the user name of the provider's `registry_auth` entry for `server_address`. |

## Example

```terraform
variable "registry_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

# Check credentials through the daemon (POST /auth) without storing anything.
ephemeral "docker_registry_login" "ghcr" {
  server_address = "ghcr.io"
  username       = "ci-bot"
  password       = var.registry_password
}

# The identity token, when the registry issues one, can replace the password
# in a later login. It is ephemeral, so pass it on only to ephemeral or
# write-only arguments.
locals {
  ghcr_status = ephemeral.docker_registry_login.ghcr.auth.status
}
```
